name: PMSA003 particulate matter sensor
description: Plantower laser-scattering dust sensor: reports PM1.0, PM2.5 and PM10 mass concentration (ug/m3, 0-500 effective range, 1 ug/m3 resolution) and particle counts per 0.1 L over a 3.3 V-logic UART at 9600 baud. Needs 4.5-5.5 V for its fan; draws up to 100 mA. Sold as: Plantower PMSA003 with its 10-pin-to-4-pin adapter board (as sold by The Pi Hut, 4-pin 2.54 mm header GND, VCC, RX, TX), with the SET and RESET pins left unbroken-out (pulled up inside the sensor).
eli5: A tiny fan pulls air past a laser and counts the dust and smoke specks, telling your board how dirty the air is.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground (pin 1, marked with an arrow on the adapter)

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 5 V (4.5-5.5 V): drives the fan. Do NOT use 3.3 V.

pins.name: RX
pins.description: Sensor serial input, 3.3 V logic: connect to the microcontroller's TX. Only needed for passive mode / sleep commands.

pins.name: TX
pins.description: Sensor serial output, 3.3 V logic, 9600 baud: connect to the microcontroller's RX

supplierQuery: Plantower PMSA003 particulate sensor with adapter board
buildNotes: Power VCC from 5 V (VIN/VBUS), not 3.3 V: the fan needs 5 V. The data pins are 3.3 V logic, so they connect straight to an ESP32 or Pico; a 5 V Arduino needs a level shifter.
Cross the serial lines: sensor TX to the microcontroller's RX, sensor RX to the microcontroller's TX. Use 9600 baud, 8N1.
After power-up the sensor is in active mode and sends a 32-byte frame by itself: about every 2.3 s when the air is steady, every 0.2-0.8 s when it changes fast.
Each frame starts 0x42 0x4D, frame length 28, then 13 big-endian 16-bit words; the last 2 bytes are the sum of the first 30. Drop frames whose sum does not match.
Use the 'atmospheric environment' values (words 4-6) for room or outdoor air; the CF=1 values (words 1-3) are meant for factory calibration.
Give it about 30 s after power-up or wake-up before trusting the numbers, and mount it with the inlet and outlet unobstructed and at least 20 cm above the floor.
The metal case is tied to GND: keep it from touching other parts of the circuit.

example.code:
from machine import UART, Pin
import time
from pmsa003 import PMSA003

uart = UART({UART_ID}, baudrate=9600, tx=Pin({RX}), rx=Pin({TX}))
sensor = PMSA003(uart)
while True:
    r = sensor.read()
    if r:
        print('PM1=%d PM2.5=%d PM10=%d ug/m3' % (r['pm1_0'], r['pm2_5'], r['pm10']))
    else:
        print('no data: check TX wiring and 5 V supply')
    time.sleep_ms(100)

test.title: Reports the PM1.0, PM2.5 and PM10 set on the sliders

library.note: Passed the Sparkbench part check in simulation and matched an independent datasheet reading (3 difference(s) settled by a third reading with quoted evidence). Not yet tested on real hardware.
